narrative:
The model estimated your probability of bad credit at 34%, meaning roughly a one-in-three chance of repayment difficulty. Although that is not a majority, it was above the bank’s acceptable risk cutoff, so your application was denied.

The strongest factor pushing the decision toward bad risk was your credit history: having no credits or all credits paid is very uncommon among approved applicants—only about 1%—and this weighed against you most heavily. The next most important factor was your checking-account status of at least 200 DM/salary, which worked in your favor as a positive signal. The third factor was the requested nine-month duration, which also helped you because it is much shorter than the approved average of about 19 months.

To improve future applications, focus on building a clearer, active credit record by using a small credit facility or secured card and paying it consistently on time. Keep your checking account in good standing, and consider asking the bank what specific credit-history evidence it would accept. A shorter loan term already helps; maintaining stable balances and a documented repayment record should strengthen your next application.
